{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2022}} {{Out of date|date=June 2025}} {{Expand list|date=February 2015}} [[File:Royal Warrant - Jenners in Edinburgh - 2004-10-22.jpg|thumbnail|250px|right|Royal Warrant awarded by [[Elizabeth II]] to [[Jenners]], a department store in [[Edinburgh]] ]] This is a list of past [[royal warrant of appointment (United Kingdom)|royal warrant of appointment]] holders of the [[British royal family]]. A full list is available [https://www.royalwarrant.org/directory here]. British royal warrants are currently granted by [[King Charles III]], [[Queen Camilla]], [[Prince William]] and [[Catherine, Princess of Wales]] to companies or tradespeople who supply goods and services. The warrant enables the supplier to advertise that they supply to the royal family. The professions, employment agencies, party planners, the media, government departments, and "places of refreshment or entertainment" (such as pubs and theatres) do not qualify.{{cite web |url=http://www.royalwarrant.org/FAQs.asp |title=FAQs |website=Royal Warrant Holders Association |accessdate=2 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080402070756/http://www.royalwarrant.org/FAQs.asp |archive-date=2 April 2008}} The [[Merchandise Marks Act 1887]] ([[50 & 51 Vict.]] c. 28) makes it illegal for companies to falsely claim that they have a royal warrant.{{cite web |url=https://archive.org/stream/merchandisemark00payngoog#page/n73/mode/2up |title=The Merchandise Marks Act 1887 |year=1888 |accessdate=4 December 2013 |page=63 |publisher=Stevens}} Following the [[Death and state funeral of Elizabeth II|death]] of [[Elizabeth II]] and the accession of [[Charles III]] in 2022, their royal warrants became void but remained valid for up to two years. Applications for new warrants from the King and [[Queen Camilla|Queen]] opened in May 2024, taking effect in 2025. ==Grantors== ;Current * [[King Charles III]] (from 2024). ** During his tenure as Prince of Wales, King Charles III granted 159 royal warrants, void but still usable for two years since his accession as king. This is a list of past royal warrant of appointment holders of the British royal family. A full list is available here. 
British royal warrants are currently granted by King Charles III, Queen Camilla, Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales to companies or tradespeople who supply goods and services. The warrant enables the supplier to advertise  that they supply to the royal family. The professions, employment agencies, party planners, the media, government departments, and "places of refreshment or entertainment" (such as pubs and theatres) do not qualify. The Merchandise Marks Act 1887 (50 & 51 Vict. c. 28) makes it illegal for companies to falsely claim that they have a royal warrant.
Following the death of Elizabeth II and the accession of Charles III in 2022, their royal warrants became void but remained valid for up to two years. Applications for new warrants from the King and Queen opened in May 2024, taking effect in 2025.
